what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Georgia in all host countries combined: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 28902 asylum seekers from Georgia.
The United States hosts the largest share, 38.2%, followed by Italy, Germany and France.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over South Ossetia territory in Georgia in 2004 and 2008, with the Republic of South Ossetia.
The fact pack records no armed conflict in Georgia in recent years, so it does not say why the number of asylum seekers grew.

when.text: UNHCR's series starts in 2000 at 1469 asylum seekers.
The figure reached its highest point, 38556, at the end of 2023, and the main years of displacement in the data are 2018 to 2019 and 2022 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took.
These are year-end totals of asylum seekers summed over every host country; refugees from Georgia are counted separately.
